correctness.rationale: The quartic equation is exact, with nonzero leading coefficient. The nonzero difference gives a unique ordered collision pair; norm-one distinct product triples are bijective with distinct preimage triples. Opposite-pair exclusion counts exactly nonextendible triples, and binomial moments reconstruct all five nonnegative integral counts. The cubic-group preimage count h is zero or gcd(3,q+1); for q=2 mod3 its value equals 3 exactly for cubic coefficients. The proof treats every odd prime power; 493 direct configurations were also evaluated independently.

value.rationale: The result completes the natural nonzero-coefficient family rather than a narrow arbitrary slice: two-thirds of all coefficients in every q=2 mod3 regime exhibit a genuinely different exact profile. It reveals a cubic-coset transition in 3- and 4-preimage fibers, while proving value-set-size invariance; this is a structural classification over infinitely many odd prime powers and not a direct renaming of the known normalized case.
